basics.name: Aleister Vaillant
basics.label: ML/CV Engineer
basics.summary: Six years of noticing that a specific tool was missing and building it. CV models trained locally and deployed to Raspberry Pi; distributed Pi infrastructure for a live immersive theater production. Asset tracking for 10,000+ hardware units. Autonomous vehicle fault triage.

work.name: StoryverseNYC
work.summary: Computer vision and Raspberry Pi infrastructure for immersive theater productions (Fairyland, AETHER).
highlights: Wrote a CV pipeline from scratch: scripted Blender to generate synthetic training data with no hand-labeling, parallelized GPU rendering across workers, fine-tuned YOLO, added Kalman filter tracking
Quantized models to TFLite INT8 (~6MB). Runs real-time on a Raspberry Pi with Arduino output control; ran live across a production with no manual annotation

Built the distributed infrastructure for a full production: a fleet of Raspberry Pis (one codebase, multiple deployable variants) coordinating an interactive show over a dedicated wifi network the system runs itself (range and channel under our control, independent of venue wifi)
Distributed video-sync: a Pi 4 coordinates a swarm of Pi Zeros driving scattered CRTs, synchronized via a leader-elected show clock and wall-clock-timestamped events; shows run up to four hours

Built a show runtime where each show is a Python program (triggers, predicates, actions), evolved from an earlier declarative config format; plus an MQTT telemetry bus and an always-on flight recorder for after-the-fact diagnosis
Built a generic Raspberry Pi image-build system with a composable module pipeline: flash and boot yields a fully configured device with no manual setup

work.name: X, the moonshot factory (Chorus)
work.summary: Python test infrastructure for prototype GPS/sensor hardware. The firmware team hired me out of ops because we'd worked well together.
highlights: Flash memory reliability test framework. Cut manual verification by 60%
BLE connectivity studies for the Product team
Proof-of-concept applications to derisk hardware approaches before committing resources

work.name: X, the moonshot factory (Chorus)
work.summary: Started in operations shipping boxes. No inventory database existed, just a provisioning spreadsheet. I built one.
highlights: Asset management system: labeled boxes, mapped devices to boxes, linked test results to device IDs. Shipping went from scanning every unit to filtering by box name. 10,000+ units tracked
Python pipeline comparing sensor measurements against ground truth. Automated report generation improved QA throughput 30%
ETL pipeline integrating the asset system into a relational database
Handled device shipping logistics for external partners

work.name: Waymo
work.summary: Triaged autonomous vehicle faults under case-volume quotas. Learned the full system architecture to make the call: hardware issue, misclassified object, or hallucination.
highlights: Reverse-engineered parts of the playback log schema. Used it to build a hard brake report
Got into the C++ source of the internal log viewer (XView), compiled locally, added hotkeys and probability displays along behavior paths

projects.name: A Long Day in Hell
projects.description: Browser-based roguelike built in 7 days. Procedurally generated infinite library where every book is deterministically derived from coordinates via base-95 bijection. ECS social simulation with 120 NPCs.
highlights: 1200+ tests, 439 commits, single self-contained HTML file
Coordinate algebra guaranteeing player's book is within navigable space by construction

projects.name: AETHER — Raspberry Pi show infrastructure
projects.description: Distributed infrastructure for a live immersive theater production: a fleet of Raspberry Pis (one codebase, several deployable variants) running an interactive show over a dedicated wifi network the system runs itself. Drift-corrected video-sync across scattered CRTs, a show runtime where each show is a Python program, MQTT telemetry, an image-build pipeline, and a flight recorder.
highlights: Video-sync: a Pi 4 coordinates a swarm of Pi Zeros driving scattered CRTs, synced via a leader show clock and wall-clock-timestamped events
Generic Pi image-build system with a composable module pipeline: flash and boot yields a fully configured device

projects.name: Eye of Maia — badge detection CV
projects.description: Real-time computer vision for immersive theater. YOLO badge detection fine-tuned on synthetic Blender data (no hand-labeling), quantized to TFLite INT8 and deployed to a Raspberry Pi with Kalman filter tracking. Ran live across a production.
